These are unmodified documents written by actual old SDK `serialize` calls on new,
synthetic configuration values. They contain no frozen TypeScript-authoring inputs.
The revision-22 native decoder must return `incompatible` before decoding either
payload. Changing a current document's revision does not replace this proof.

- `revision20-synthetic.sdk-document`: matched revision-20 SDK/addon baseline, copied from
  `implementation/implementer/baseline/revision20-synthetic.json` in the
  `/private/tmp/2026-11-case-byte-binding/` job home.
  SHA-256: `745352414fdf39fa6614e12173588ac7b868ab24db0e22225b4caca171961ee9`.
- `revision21-synthetic.sdk-document`: matched revision-21 SDK/addon normal consumer,
  copied from `implementation/verifier/revision21-synthetic.json` in that job home.
  SHA-256: `912407069a2312231c04bcda5adcc234f9df444e6fcbae132b83daf4b2122109`.

Their source roots and loopback endpoints are inert authored strings. The test
reads these documents through the native codec; it does not run their configuration.
